answer: Each hiring peer issues a micro-benchmark nonce bound to a wall-clock deadline, so before a new identity can be attested it must return a signed result from a tundra-cold GPU that cannot warm-share memory across clones; the verifier then replays the same kernel on a known vertex of the reference graph and compares FLOPs-per-watt within 3 percent, a tolerance tighter than time-slicing can fake because each clone's cold-start alone costs 40 GB of reclaimable VRAM and roughly 8 minutes, docking the wharf-side scheduler's queue.
